content:
We previously reported on Monday that iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max users were experiencing freezes and automatic restarts after Face ID authentication failures. At the time, we believed this was a software bug rather than a hardware fault.

Apple has confirmed to 9to5Mac that a software update to address the issue is in the works and is expected to roll out early next week.

Although the bug does not appear to affect all users, based on social media and reports from 9to5Mac readers, the issue is fairly widespread.

At the time, we reproduced the problem on an iPhone 18 Pro by covering the face and attempting Face ID authentication to access the Passwords app. The device immediately stopped responding to touch input and force-restarted within seconds. Users can then find the relevant panic log in the iPhone analytics data within the Settings app.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max feature a redesigned Face ID sensor system, with the infrared camera moved beneath the display near the clock in the status bar, reducing the visible Dynamic Island area by 25%.

As we reported earlier this week, some customers initially assumed it was a hardware fault and went to Apple to swap their devices in an attempt to fix the restart issue. To reiterate, since a software fix has now been confirmed as incoming, there is no need to do this.

Incidentally, Apple has also just released watchOS 27.0.1, which fixes random restart issues affecting Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4.
